_status_note: NOT LOADABLE AND NOT GENERATABLE. `generate.mjs` refuses this file on `source-not-transcribed` and on `exception-list-not-transcribed`, deliberately and by design. The shape, the coverage bounds and the session rule are settled and reviewable here; the VALUES are not present because the CME publication could not be retrieved in the session that wrote this file (see README.md, `The retrieval that did not happen`). NULL IS NOT THE EMPTY LIST: `holidays: null` says nobody has read the publication, `holidays: []` would assert the exchange closes on no day of the year and would load clean while making every counter advance through Christmas. This is ADR-042 F-1's lesson, that a holiday is a positive fact rather than an absence, applied one layer earlier to the file. ADR-055 WIDENED THE SHAPE ON 2026-08-17 and this file carries the widening without carrying any value: every holiday entry gains a required `absorbs_into` with its own three states (see `_holidays_note`), and `coverage` gains `evidence_to`. The generator now also refuses this file on `coverage-evidence-not-transcribed`, which is a third independent refusal rather than a spare: `status` says nobody has transcribed, the null lists say nobody has read the exceptions, and `evidence_to` says nobody has established how far the evidence reaches. They can be satisfied one at a time and a file that satisfies two of the three is still refused.

provenance._note: ADR-042 verbatim: source URL, retrieval date, the retrieved artifact committed beside it, and its SHA-256. `artifact` names a file in this directory. `artifact_sha256` is the digest of THE BYTES THE EXCHANGE SERVED, and it is NOT the digest the loader writes to `trading_calendar_loads.source_digest`, which is the digest of THIS FILE. Both are needed and neither substitutes for the other.

coverage._note: ADR-042 OQ-SE-02, AMENDED ON ITS MECHANISM BY ADR-055 SECTION 5. The old reason for `to` was a fact about the publisher, that the current year plus two is about as far as CME publishes. That premise was put in question by FINDING 2 and ADR-055 deliberately declines to decide it, because it is legible only from a paste. The rule is now an EVIDENCE BOUND, which is true whatever CME publishes: `to` MAY NOT EXCEED `evidence_to`. Inclusive bounds, in exchange CT trading-day space, the same domain as `trading_calendar.trading_day`, never a UTC calendar date derived from a timestamp. The horizon alarm warns when coverage runs less than six months ahead, and against an evidence-bounded horizon it fires when the transcribed calendar actually runs short rather than never firing against a declared-but-empty tail.
coverage._evidence_to_note: THE LAST DATE WHOSE EXCEPTIONS COME FROM A COMMITTED ARTIFACT. ADR-055 section 5: declaring coverage through 2028 while filling only 2026 makes `trading_calendar_loads` assert knowledge nobody has, which is the state ADR-042 F-4 exists to make impossible. NULL IS NOT A FAR HORIZON: null says nobody has established how far the evidence reaches, and `generate.mjs` refuses the file on `coverage-evidence-not-transcribed`. A date says the artifacts in this directory carry every exception up to and including it. `to` above is 2028-12-31 and is therefore UNSATISFIABLE until this value reaches it, which is deliberate: the five committed artifacts are three-day windows covering four holidays, the holiday list itself has still not been retrieved, and the honest declarable coverage today is nothing.

session_rule._note: P1 S-E section 3.1, verbatim: every weekday inside coverage that is not a holiday, 17:00 CT on the prior calendar day to 16:00 CT on the trading day. This lives in the file rather than in the generator because a rule that changes should move as a reviewed data change, not as a code edit that silently rewrites every historical row on the next regeneration. `open_day_offset: -1` is why Monday's session opens on Sunday evening.

_holidays_note:
EVERY HOLIDAY ENTRY CARRIES `day`, `name` AND `absorbs_into`. ADR-055: a holiday does not remove a session, it PAUSES THE SESSION BELONGING TO THE NEXT TRADE DATE, and that session opened before the holiday began. CME opens trade date 2026-09-08 on Sunday 09-06, not Monday; `session_rule` computes Monday and is wrong by twenty-four hours, so a fill on the Sunday evening of Labor Day weekend lands inside NO MERIT SESSION AT ALL, which is the condition R-01 exists to detect.

THE KEY IS `day` AND NOT `date`. ADR-055 section 3's illustrative snippet writes `date`; `readHolidays` in generate.mjs has parsed `h.day` since it was written, and this file follows the merged code rather than the snippet. The ADR rules `absorbs_into`; it does not rule a rename.

`absorbs_into` HAS THREE STATES AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE DESIGN:
  ABSENT  refused as `absorbs-into-not-transcribed`. Nobody has read the artifact for this holiday
  null    the POSITIVE STATEMENT that this holiday absorbs no session. The next trade date opens by `session_rule`. A Friday holiday is this shape: 12-24 carries `12:15 (CLOSED)` and nothing after it, in all nine futures classes, and that empty evening is EVIDENCE rather than missing coverage
  object  the explicit bounds of the absorbed session, read off the artifact under TR-01 and NEVER computed
That is the same distinction this file already draws between `holidays: null` and `holidays: []`, which is ADR-042 F-1's lesson one layer deeper.

THE OBJECT CARRIES FIVE KEYS: `trading_day`, `session_open_day`, `session_open_ct`, `session_close_day`, `session_close_ct`.

THE CLOSE IS CARRIED ALTHOUGH IT IS DERIVABLE, AND CARRYING IT IS DELIBERATE. It is 16:00, or the `early_closes` entry when the absorbing trade date is an early close, as Thanksgiving's 11-27 12:15 is. Two independent statements of one fact is this file's `declared` pattern, whose own note says two independent statements of one number is the point of stating it twice. NEITHER STATEMENT IS AUTHORITATIVE ALONE: the transcriber states the bounds from the exchange, generate.mjs derives what it expects, and a disagreement is `absorbed-close-disagrees`. The derivation is DEMOTED TO A CROSS-CHECK rather than discarded, which is the one role it can hold safely: ADR-055 section 2 shows the natural walk-back derivation computing a Thursday 12-24 17:00 open for trade date 12-28, which the Christmas artifact positively contradicts.

THE INTRADAY PAUSE IS NOT RECORDED AND THAT IS A DECISION. Trade date 2026-09-08 halts Monday 12:00 to 17:00. A PREOPEN accepts orders and matches none, so the outer span is a SUPERSET of the tradeable time and R-01 only ever asks whether a fill fell OUTSIDE. Ordinary days already carry unrecorded pauses (`Grains` shows 07:45 PAUSED). ADR-055 section 4, and a field nothing reads is session 49's `sessions[].kind` landmine.

EXAMPLE, FOR SHAPE ONLY, NOT A CLAIM ABOUT WHAT CME PUBLISHES:
  { "day": "2026-09-07", "name": "Labor Day", "absorbs_into": { "trading_day": "2026-09-08", "session_open_day": "2026-09-06", "session_open_ct": "17:00", "session_close_day": "2026-09-08", "session_close_ct": "16:00" } }
  { "day": "2026-12-25", "name": "Christmas", "absorbs_into": null }

declared._note: The transcriber's own count, stated independently of the lists so the two must agree. `checkRows` rejects a disagreement on `declared-count-disagrees`. Two independent statements of one number is the point of stating it twice, and it is the check that catches a row deleted while editing.
